meta.notes: Prompts only. No answers or rarity yet; answers to come from Wikipedia scraping plus LLM guidance. judge_score is 1-10 enjoyment from an independent judge agent. overlap_groups lists pairs/groups the judge thought overlap; high = keep one, medium = fine if never on the same day. v2 (James, 2026-11-25): cut every prompt scoring 4 or below, the number-system overlap, and pop-culture prompts with no tech or maths link (video games stay). See removed_v2. v3 (James, 2026-11-25): every prompt rated for clarity (1 = clear on first read, 2 = an example helps, 3 = vague without one) and given a 'like ...' example unless clarity is 1; the example is a common answer, so the game may want to score it as Bit or block it. est_answers is a rough count of valid answers from the Wikipedia source; every kept prompt is 50+. Prompts under 50 were merged into a broader prompt or cut (see removed_v3). v4 (James, 2026-11-25): removed 40 selected prompts and added "Name a Greek letter". Removed the inventor prompt at James’s request.
dropped_placeholders: type (primitive data type: tiny closed set)

overlap_groups.why: SHA-256 and MD5 are top answers for both hash functions and modern crypto algorithms.
CRC and checksums are typed for both hash functions and error-detecting codes.
The lossy half of compression (JPEG, MP3, H.264) is the same as the codec set.
Brute force, dictionary and rainbow-table attacks fit both prompts.
Caesar, Vigenere and Playfair are likely typed as famous codes too.
2FA, MFA and passwords are top answers for both authentication and security defence.
FizzBuzz is the canonical answer to both the beginner exercise and interview problem prompts.
Paging, virtual memory, deadlock, semaphores and threads are top OS-concept answers that also fill memory and concurrency prompts.
MVC, microservices and layered architecture are typed as both patterns and architecture styles.
npm, Maven, Gradle, Cargo sit in both package manager and build tool sets.
Express and similar JS frameworks are valid and top-of-mind for both.
USB, PCIe, SATA, Thunderbolt and HDMI are top answers for both ports and buses.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee and NFC are typed as both protocols and wireless technologies.
WhatsApp, Discord, Telegram and Snapchat fit both social media and messaging.
Slack, Teams and Discord are top answers for both messaging and team collaboration tools.
Turing, von Neumann and Godel are top answers for both computer scientists and mathematicians.
Galileo, Kepler, Newton, Hubble and Sagan fit both physicists and astronomers.
Googol and googolplex are headline answers for both prompts.
Torus and sphere are top 3D-shape answers and also the core famous surfaces.
Complete, bipartite, planar and tree graphs are both named graph families and graph-theory terms.
Vector space, metric space and topological space blur algebraic structures and mathematical spaces.
Gradient descent, Newton's method and simulated annealing are typed for both.
Monty Hall, birthday paradox, St Petersburg and Bertrand paradoxes fill both sets.
Gambler's fallacy, sunk cost and confirmation bias are typed for both fallacies and biases.
Space Shuttle, Soyuz, Starship and Dragon are typed for both rockets and spacecraft.
GG, AFK, noob and pwned are top answers for both internet and gamer slang.
Tron and The Matrix lead both computer films and CGI films.
The Imitation Game is the top answer for both films about computers and about scientists.
Warp drive, teleporter, time machine and FTL are typed as both fictional tech and sci-fi tropes.
Green Hill Zone, Rainbow Road and Hyrule-style places are both locations and famous levels.
Hades, Binding of Isaac, Spelunky and Dead Cells are top answers for both.
PlayStation and Xbox (and their networks) are typed as gaming platforms, overlapping consoles.
Modulo, exponentiation, addition and bitwise ops appear in both operation and operator sets.
regedit, cmd.exe, Task Manager and System32 tools blur Windows tools and system files.
Bletchley Park and the Computer History Museum are top answers for both.
Spaghetti code, god object and cargo cult are typed as both code smells and jargon.
